title: Learning from Their Daughters: Family Exposure to Gender Disparity and Female Representation in Male-Led Ventures
authors: Zhiyan Wu; Lucia Naldi; Karl J. Wennberg; Timurs Umans
near_miss_reason: The only main-text staggered specification (Figure 2 event study around the first childbirth, girl vs boy) adds time-varying controls (founderMarried, founderEdu, lventurePerformance, lfirmSize) in both panels. The control-free static TWFE (Table A2-2 M1, M3) is appendix-only. In addition, the package ships made-up synthetic data only.
eligible_reason: Event-study sample: male founders with one child whose first child is born during 2004-2017. Treatment DiD = 1(first child is a girl) x 1(year >= birth year): binary, absorbing, switching on at founder-specific birth years (many cohorts); founders of boys are never treated. Founder FE + year FE. Main tables (3a-6c) are pooled cross-sectional OLS of female representation on the number of daughters (count) with industry-year and number-of-children FE, not DiD.
design_notes: Do files/Do estimates/1 - Do estimates to produce tables and figures.do, section 'Figures and Tables in the Event Study Analysis' (lines 848-1045): keep childNumber<=1, founders with first birth observed in sample and at least one pre and one post year; treat = max(girlNumber); yearRelativeToShock binned at <=-5 and >=4; treat_v = event_v x treat, treat_1 (the <=-5 bin) omitted. Figure 2: xtreg femaleDirectorRatio $controlVariables i.year treat_*, fe (director panel) and xtreg femaleEmployeeRatio $controlVariables i.industry_year treat_*, fe (employee panel); cluster founder. Table A2-2 (appendix): xtreg y i.year DiD, fe (M1 director, M3 employee) and with controls (M2, M4). Main Tables 3a-6c: reg y i.industry_year i.childNumber $controlVariables girlNumber.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Birth-year cohorts 2005-2016 likely; cannot count on real data (synthetic file only).
